questions.text: A 5'6" female patient is intubated and needs to be placed on mechanical ventilation. What is her IBW and appropriate initial tidal volume range?

answers.text: IBW ≈ 58 kg; initial Vt 350–465 mL (6–8 mL/kg)
IBW ≈ 58 kg; initial Vt 580–780 mL (10–13 mL/kg)
IBW ≈ 73 kg; initial Vt 440–585 mL (6–8 mL/kg)
Use actual body weight; initial Vt 600–800 mL for any adult female

questions.text: An ARDS patient's plateau pressure climbs to 33 cmH₂O on a tidal volume of 7 mL/kg IBW. What is the most appropriate next step?

answers.text: Reduce tidal volume to 4–6 mL/kg IBW and target Pplat < 28 cmH₂O
Increase PEEP to recruit alveoli and lower Pplat
Increase inspiratory flow rate to shorten I-Time
Switch to pressure control to allow Pplat to self-limit

questions.text: A 6'0" male patient (IBW = 80 kg) is ventilated at Vt 900 mL, RR 12, PaCO₂ = 40 mmHg. You need to correct his Vt to 480 mL. What new RR maintains the same minute volume?

answers.text: RR = 22–23 breaths/min (current MV 10.8 L ÷ 0.480 L)
RR = 18 breaths/min
RR = 12 breaths/min — no change needed since PaCO₂ is normal
RR = 16 breaths/min

questions.text: An adult patient is ventilated with a peak pressure of 40 cmH₂O. Approximately how much volume is lost to circuit compressible volume?

answers.text: 120 mL (40 cmH₂O × 3 mL/cmH₂O)
60 mL (40 cmH₂O × 1.5 mL/cmH₂O)
20 mL (40 cmH₂O × 0.5 mL/cmH₂O)
80 mL — a fixed value for all adult circuits

questions.text: A patient's VD/Vt ratio is calculated at 0.64. What does this indicate?

answers.text: Significant lung disease — 64% of each breath is wasted dead space, predicting high mortality risk
Normal dead space fraction — no intervention is needed
The patient is hyperventilating and blowing off too much CO₂
Exercise-induced increase in alveolar ventilation

questions.text: A patient's PaCO₂ is 55 mmHg on RR 12 and Vt 500 mL. Using the PaCO₂ correction formula, what new RR is needed to achieve a target PaCO₂ of 40 mmHg?

answers.text: RR = 14 breaths/min
RR = 20 breaths/min
Increase tidal volume rather than rate to lower PaCO₂

questions.text: You are adjusting FiO₂ and PEEP for a patient with refractory hypoxemia. In what order should these settings be adjusted to correct a low PaO₂?

answers.text: Increase FiO₂ to 60% first, then add PEEP; if PEEP causes cardiac compromise, return to increasing FiO₂ above 60%
Increase PEEP first to 10 cmH₂O, then increase FiO₂
Increase FiO₂ to 100% immediately, then wean PEEP
Adjust PEEP and FiO₂ simultaneously in equal increments

questions.text: What PEEP contraindication is an immediate safety concern requiring the PEEP to be minimized?

answers.text: Untreated tension pneumothorax
Mild pulmonary hypertension
ARDS with a P/F ratio of 180
Moderate refractory hypoxemia with FiO₂ already at 60%

questions.text: Increasing the peak inspiratory flow rate (PIFR) in volume-control ventilation has which combined effect?

answers.text: Shortens I-Time, increases E-Time, increases PIP, and worsens gas distribution
Lengthens I-Time, decreases E-Time, decreases PIP, and improves gas distribution
Increases tidal volume without changing I-Time or PIP
Decreases PaCO₂ by increasing minute ventilation

questions.text: A ventilated patient triggers a high-pressure alarm that was set at 45 cmH₂O. The clinician notes PIP is 47 cmH₂O, which is up from 32 cmH₂O an hour ago. Pplat is 28 cmH₂O. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: Increased airway resistance — the large PIP–Pplat gap indicates obstruction (secretions or bronchospasm)
Decreased compliance — elevated Pplat would accompany elevated PIP
Circuit disconnection — low pressure alarm would trigger instead
Auto-PEEP — would cause elevated Pplat and baseline pressure

questions.text: In which clinical scenario is an inversed I:E ratio (2:1) most appropriate?

answers.text: ARDS — prolonged inspiration recruits collapsed alveoli and improves oxygenation
Severe COPD exacerbation — more time is needed for exhalation to prevent air trapping
Post-operative patient with normal lungs — reduces WOB during early recovery
Drug overdose — shortens I-Time to reduce sedation requirements

questions.text: What is the purpose of Automatic Tube Compensation (ATC) in pressure support?

answers.text: Automatically calculates and applies the minimum PS needed to overcome the resistance of the specific ETT size
Compensates for circuit leaks by adjusting tidal volume delivery
Adjusts PEEP automatically based on real-time compliance measurements
Increases IPAP when the patient's spontaneous tidal volume falls below target
